steps.text: Gather the ingredients. Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease a 9x5-inch loaf pan.
Combine flour, sugar, baking powder, salt, and baking soda in a large bowl. Add cranberries and walnuts; stir until well coated.
Mix together orange juice, egg, oil, and zest in a medium bowl until combined. Pour over flour mixture; stir until just blended. Spoon batter into the prepared loaf pan.
Bake in the preheated oven until a toothpick inserted into the center of loaf comes out clean, about 50 minutes. Let cool in the pan briefly before removing to a wire rack to cool completely.

raw_recipe.headline: Cranberry Nut Bread
raw_recipe.description: This cranberry nut bread is moist and easy to make with fresh cranberries, walnuts, orange juice, and zest for a flavorful festive quick bread.
raw_recipe.name: Cranberry Nut Bread

review.reviewBody:
This is such a delicious quick bread. I really like the suggestion of one reviewer who wrote that she left the cranberries whole... that way you get the maximum flavor. I quess my only (very small) complaint about this bread was that I wanted more cranberries. I would probably double the amount next time. Thank you Karin for submitting this recipe!

p.s. I made another batch and baked it as mini loaves... recipe made 4; they were done in 25 min.... love this recipe!

This bread was wonderful! After greasing the pan, I sprinkled cinnamon and sugar in the pan to give the crust a sweet crunch. I sprinkled some extra chopped walnuts and some "sugar in the raw" on top before baking, and it really does look like a picture! Tastes great and a beautiful holiday bread. Takes no time to whip together too!
Very tasty, fruity bread. I doubled the recipe and baked it in "little loaf" pans, 5 3/4 x 3 x 2 1/8, for 30 minutes. It made 5 little loaves.

This is so good! I made it on Thanksgiving day, and everyone love it. My husband love it so much that he went to the market to grab me 2 more bags of cranberries. ^^ I also try to make it using the muffin pan and baked in the oven for about 22 mins, and it came out good as well.

This was a good recipe and I gave it four stars because I did numerous modifications which I believe elevated the flavor. I used 1/2 cup of brown sugar (not 3/4 cup of white sugar); added a teaspoon of cinnamon; used 1/4 cup of melted unsalted butter (rather than the oil); two cups of cranberries (rather than 1 cup); did a simple confectioners sugar/orange extract glaze. Baked for 52 minutes in my oven and it came out tasty. Husband loves it.

I made this recipe into muffins! I did take the advice from a previous poster and doubled the cranberries ( used 2 cups). I also used a 1/4 c brown sugar, 1/4 c chopped walnuts, and 1/2 teaspoon of cinnamon mixed together and placed on top of the muffins before baking. They are absolutely perfect!

I reduced the salt to 1/2t. and cut the cranberries in half with kitchen shears. All ingredients were mixed according to the directions. The batter is a little thick, so I 'm glad I blended everything by hand and didn't risk over mixing it with an electric mixer. The batter filled three Pampered Chef mini loaf pans. Bake for 35-40 minutes.

Easy, quick and delicious! The only change to the recipe I made was I used frozen whole cranberries instead. I didn’t chop them. The zest got left out because I didn’t have an orange. I used 3 small loaf pans and 40 min. baking time. First time making this recipe, it certainly won’t be the last! Yum Yum Yummy!

Needs a touch more moisture...I added 1/4 c pineapple juice (what I had onhand) and check for doneness @ 45-50 minutes...or bread could be dry. I make this every holiday season for all of my friends and neighbors....Will also make 3 small foil pans of bread!

This is almost the same as my old recipe. I use no oil I use 2 tablespoon butter.. I use 2 cups of cranberries chop them real rough and add some to top before baking. . I use a cup of rough chopped walnuts. I also use the rind from one large orange and squeeze the juice from that orange but add some to make the 3/4 cup. 
Great and moist recipe. Can make muffins with same recipe.
Enjoy!! Nana

Excellent and Easy. This is the recipe on the back of the cranberry bags. Other than doubling the amount to 2 cups of berries and keeping them whole, I don't change a thing. Don't overbake. 50 min. exactly is right. If the dough is too stiff, add a few tablespoon of milk to moisten it up. TIP - for a prettier bread, place some cranberries on top of the batter before you bake it. The red color on top adds a gorgeous appearance to the bread. I also glaze mine with a lemon glaze. The glaze gives it a little tart flavor on top and keeps the bread moist. (glaze - lemon juice and powdered sugar). Glaze while warm.

I used about a 1/4 cup of more cranberries and probably more zest but the basic recipe stayed the same. I used dried cranberries and didn't read down to see the note that I should have soaked them in water first but it was delicious anyway. I probably will soak the cranberries next time but its hard to imagine that it could be any better. Moist, rose perfectly 50 min at 350 was also just right. I can't say enough but I'll make this again, in fact I'm making another loaf today to take it to church on Sunday. The bonus is it was very easy and worth every effort. Yummy delicious!!
Served at church luncheon and this cranberry bread was a hit!
Easy and tasty with a crisp top and soft, moist inside. I made mine with the left-over cranberries from my canned Christmas cranberry sauce. Turned out really well.
When you "PRINT" recipe the 2 tablespoons of oil is not there! ugh, I printed it, followed the directions, and it did not come out great because of the typo in the printed version

Lost the inherited family recipe and I think this is better, so I’m counting that a blessing. I made a few personal choice adjustments; added cinnamon, a small box of instant vanilla pudding ( I do this when multiplying a recipe as I tripled this one). I used a nut medley of walnuts, almonds, & hazelnuts finely ground. This will be my go to as long as I can still bake, thank you for sharing it ❤️

Really great! I did add some pumpkin pie spice (I add it to all things Holiday)and vanilla. I also had doubled the recipe, so I didn't have enough orange juice and I added some pineapple juice to make up the difference and this came out delicious! I like to bake my "breads" just just just until they're done and not over at all and these weren't super brown but still really wonderful. The cranberries were nice and tart and the walnuts (which I toasted before adding) were the perfect savory crunchy addition. That with the orange and spices made this excellent. I will be keeping this recipe and making it again! Update: I made these again and I did have enough oranges for all the juice and I have to say that tho they are still excellent, the pineapple juice I added before gave this a kind of "stickier" (in the best way) texture. I think I will continue to use the pineapple juice, but really excellent either way!
I made this with gf flour, King Arthur’s all purpose flour. I also added 3/4 teaspoon xantham gum. Turned out perfect I added about a 1/4 cup more of cranberries, wanted more in my bread. Love it!!!
Great to see this recipe, it was one of mt mother's favorite for Christmas morning.
Simple & the outcome outstanding, a new family favourite for sure!
